item.title: Brazil reduces fragmented native vegetation area by 43% over 38 years
item.description:
The area of native vegetation fragmented by deforestation for land-use change in Brazil has decreased by 43 percent over 38 years, as per data from the Degradation module of MapBiomas, released this Thursday (Oct. 29).

Brazil went from 287 hectares of fragmented forest in 1986 to 163 hectares in 2024. These are patches of original forest surrounded by areas cleared for agriculture, pasture, or urban development.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Amazon records lowest deforestation level in 41 years.
  • Brazil’s Cerrado loses 13.9M hectares of riverbank vegetation.
  • Luxembourg joins Tropical Forest Forever Facility.
Even though the total fragmented area has decreased, these patches have become smaller while their number has increased. There were 2.35 million patches of native vegetation in 1986, rising to 3.41 million in 2024.

According to Dhemerson Conciani, a researcher at the Amazon Environmental Research Institute (Ipam), these small fragments hinder seed dispersal and animal movement, directly affecting the reproduction of native species living in these areas. Conciani is also the technical coordinator of the Degradation Group at MapBiomas.

“[This fragmentation] reduces gene flow [the transfer of genetic material] and increases the risk of local extinctions.”

Biomes

When the data are broken down by biome, the Atlantic forest is the most affected, with 1.38 million fragmented areas, and the cerrado ranks second, comprising 957,000 small patches of native vegetation.

The Atlantic forest also contains the smallest fragments, with an average area of 25 hectares. With an average area of 81 hectares, the pampa is the second-most fragmented biome, followed by the cerrado, where fragments average 105 hectares.

In the Amazon, although the fragments will be the largest in terms of area by 2024 – at 662 hectares – their size has decreased by 76 percent since 1986, when the average fragment size was 2,700 hectares.

The number of isolated fragments separated by deforested areas has also increased over 38 years, rising from 144,000 fragments in 1986 to 519,000 in 2024 – a 260 percent surge.

“The more fragmented the landscape becomes, the smaller the average area of its fragments, and this is terrible in environmental terms because it drastically increases exposure to edge effects and fire, especially in years with extreme weather events,” Conciani stated.

Vulnerability

Edge areas are strips of land adjacent (30 to 150 meters) to deforested regions that suffer the effects of degradation because they are subjected to conditions different from those in preserved areas – such as excessive sunlight, vulnerability to strong winds, and soil siltation due to moisture loss.

According to researchers, 37 million to 102 million hectares of native vegetation are located in these edge zones across Brazil. This represents 7 to 18 percent of the country’s native vegetation.

Among the Brazilian biomes, the cerrado has the largest area of native vegetation exposed to the vulnerabilities of edge zones. It spans 11 million to 32 million hectares. In terms of proportion, however, the Atlantic forest is the most exposed biome, with 29 to 66 percent of its total remaining native vegetation located in edge zones.

COP17

The study was presented this Thursday (29) in Yerevan, Armenia, during the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

According to GeoKarten researcher Eduardo Vélez, who is also a member of the MapBiomas Degradation Group, understanding the dynamics of native vegetation loss and fragmentation is key to addressing the global biodiversity crisis.

“The previously unpublished and updated information on the fragmentation of native vegetation in Brazil is crucial for understanding the scale of the problem, preventing it from worsening, and even guiding restoration efforts aimed at achieving greater ecological connectivity.”

item.title: Flávio’s campaign coordinator: No evidence of election fraud
item.description:
Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), the Senate opposition leader and Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign coordinator, commented on the candidate’s release of a letter described as coup-mongering. Flávio fled to the US with his family after losing the presidential election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

In an initial version of the letter, posted on X on Wednesday (Oct. 28), Flávio Bolsonaro declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the original post was deleted and replaced with a revised version that changed “president-elect” to “leader of Brazil.”

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Coup-mongering letter: Flávio Bolsonaro thanks Trump, Milei for aid.
  • On Flávio Bolsonaro’s letter, Trump says he will not “get involved”.
  • Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.
“The letter posted on his Twitter [X] account - which is an official letter, the definitive version - presents him as a leader. In fact, given the number of votes he received and the role he played in the last election, Flávio is now the leading figure of the right in Brazil,” Marinho said at a press conference in the Senate. “I believe there must have been some problem with the drafting of the letter,” he added, referring to the change in wording.

When asked whether there had been fraud in Brazil’s election - a claim Flávio Bolsonaro makes without providing evidence in the letter - Rogério Marinho acknowledged that he had no evidence to support it.

“The PL cannot make that claim, nor can I, because there is no evidence to support it,” he acknowledged.

Marinho described Flávio Bolsonaro’s accusation in the letter as an emotional outburst following his decision to leave the country. He also referred to Flávio Bolsonaro as an “exile,” although the senator left Brazil voluntarily and without an arrest warrant.

He is under investigation in several cases involving alleged money laundering, currency evasion, and corruption.

In one of these cases, he is suspected of money laundering through betting platforms alongside attorney Willer Tomaz. He is also the subject of an investigation into the financing of Dark Horse, a film chronicling his father’s career. Starting next year, his Senate term will come to an end, and he will lose his privileged jurisdiction and parliamentary immunity.

Rogério Marinho also commented on US President Donald Trump’s statement that he “will not get involved” in the controversy surrounding Flávio Bolsonaro’s coup-mongering letter. The allied senator said Trump has the right to express his views on international politics but stressed that Brazil must resolve its own problems, rejecting foreign intervention.

“I hope there will be no intervention in Brazil’s internal affairs,” Marinho added.

item.title: Former Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro charged in fraud case
item.description:
On Wednesday (Oct. 28), Brazil’s Federal Police charged former banker Daniel Vorcaro and 14 others under investigation for financial fraud at the state-owned Banco Regional de Brasília (BRB). The irregularities were brought under scrutiny during the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero.

The police report states that Vorcaro played a “personal, repeated, and directive role” in transactions involving irregular loan portfolios at Banco Master that caused losses to BRB.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Top court to rule if Justice Moraes can be probed in bank fraud case.
  • Lula urges full disclosure on Brazil’s “biggest financial crime”.
  • Billions frozen in crackdown on Brazil’s biggest bank fraud case.
“As the controlling shareholder of Banco Master, Vorcaro stood at the center of decision-making within the framework under investigation and was the primary economic beneficiary of the transactions intended to secure liquidity for the institution,” the Federal Police concluded.

He was arrested in March this year and is being held at the Papudinha prison in the Federal District.

In addition to Vorcaro, the list of those charged also includes former BRB President Paulo Henrique Costa and Augusto Lima, a former partner at Master.

All those under investigation have been charged with fraudulent management of a financial institution, criminal organization, and money laundering.

Losses

According to the federal investigators, the losses already determined amount to some BRL 2.7 billion. Part of the losses was caused by nonexistent loan portfolios held in the name of Tirreno, a shell company operated by Master, which conducted transactions with BRB.

“There are, therefore, some BRL 2.7 billion in losses that have already been formally documented and acknowledged. This is not an abstract estimate or a merely contingent risk,” the Federal Police stated.

After concluding the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero, investigators submitted the report to Brazil’s prosecutor-general and requested that the Supreme Court extend the probes for an additional 60 days.

The extension will be used to complete the pending forensic examinations and to submit a supplementary investigative report.

The Other Side

In a statement, Daniel Vorcaro’s defense team denied that BRB’s transactions with Tirreno caused any losses to the state-owned bank.

According to the lawyers, “the deal involving Tirreno’s portfolios was not finalized. The portfolios were replaced by other assets, and the exchange that took place demonstrates that the transactions between Banco Master and BRB generated positive results for Banco de Brasília. No official forensic investigation has found any loss,” the defense stated.

item.title: Coup-mongering letter: Flávio Bolsonaro thanks Trump, Milei for aid
item.description:
After fleeing Brazil for the United States, defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter thanking Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump for their support in helping him escape the country.

In an initial version of the coup-mongering letter, the senator declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the wording was changed to “leader of Brazil.”

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
In the letter, the defeated candidate alleges, without providing evidence, that Brazil’s election was rigged. He also criticizes Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting hours until 7 p.m., following a request from the campaigns of both the Liberal Party and the Workers’ Party.

Flávio Bolsonaro was defeated by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the presidential runoff held last Sunday (Oct. 25), with Lula receiving 64 million votes. Flávio Bolsonaro, meanwhile, received just over 59 million votes. The two-hour extension of voting hours accounted for only 34,393 votes. According to the Superior Electoral Court, approximately 158.7 million Brazilian voters were eligible to vote.

“A decision by the Superior Electoral Court, which overstepped its authority, extended voting at the eleventh hour. The order arrived only after the legal voting hours had ended and the polls had already closed,” Flávio Bolsonaro complained.

His claims contradict the Superior Electoral Court’s official vote count and certification of the election. The outcome was also recognized by the Organization of American States (OAS) and leaders from countries across several continents. Flávio Bolsonaro’s own party, the Liberal Party (PL), also acknowledged Lula’s victory.

In the letter, Flávio Bolsonaro also criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’s decision to bar him from leaving the country and order the seizure of his personal and diplomatic passports. Moraes issued the order at the request of the Federal Police, which cited the risk that the senator might flee amid investigations into alleged money laundering and currency evasion.

Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation in two cases before the Supreme Court. In one, he and attorney Willer Tomaz are suspected of money laundering through betting platforms. He is also under investigation over the financing of Dark Horse, a film about his father’s career.

In a statement released by his press office, he said he would lead the opposition from the US.

Escape

The senator arrived in Miami, Florida, with his wife and two daughters on Wednesday morning (28), following a day of uncertainty about his whereabouts. The family crossed into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, which connects Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil, with Puerto Iguazú, Argentina. At 11:30 p.m., they boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador, before continuing on to the US.

Democrats

On Wednesday morning (28), the US House Foreign Affairs Committee criticized the Trump administration for granting a visa to Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

On social media, the committee, which is aligned with the Democratic Party, contrasted current US immigration policies toward people fleeing conflict with the treatment of Flávio Bolsonaro and his family.

“No asylum for people fleeing the war in Sudan or conflicts in Haiti, but [Secretary of State Marco] Rubio is rolling out the red carpet for Bolsonaro,” the committee said in a post on X.

item.title: On Flávio Bolsonaro’s letter, Trump says he will not “get involved”
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday (Oct. 28) that he “will not get involved” when asked about a coup-mongering letter released by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in which he declared himself the “true president-elect of the country.” Half an hour later, the senator changed the wording to “leader of Brazil.”

Trump confirmed that the US had granted visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and once again questioned the integrity of Brazil’s electoral process without providing evidence.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro rejects Lula’s victory, seeks to annul election.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
“I’m not going to comment on that, but I know we gave him authorization to enter the country. I’m not going to get involved. It was a very strange election, that’s for sure,” Trump said.

Earlier, after fleeing Brazil for the United States, Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter thanking Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump for their support in helping him escape the country.

In the document, the defeated candidate alleges, without providing evidence, that Brazil’s election was rigged. He also criticizes Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting hours until 7 p.m., following a request from the campaigns of the Liberal Party (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro’s party, and the Workers’ Party (PT), Lula’s party.
item.dc:creator: Agência Brasil

item.title: Lula terms Flávio Bolsonaro’s escape “shameful”
item.description:
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on Tuesday (Oct. 27) described Flávio Bolsonaro’s escape to the US as “shameful.” In the opinion of the president, who was reelected last Sunday (Oct. 25), his opponent at the polls is in debt to the justice system.

“A citizen who secretly flees his country does so because he must have something to hide,” said Lula.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Aircraft carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family lands in US.
“This act of leaving Brazil is shameful. He should have turned in his passport. The Federal Police must have already suspected he would leave Brazil – he is under investigation,” he added.

Lula welcomed supporters who had gathered to celebrate his 81st birthday outside the Alvorada Palace, the president’s official residence. There, he cut a cake and gave a speech.

The president recalled the time he himself was arrested in April 2018, when he handed over his passport and turned himself in to the Federal Police.

“I decided to turn myself in to the Federal Police because I wanted to expose my accusers and prove my innocence,” he said. At the time, Lula spent 580 days in prison and was released on November 8, 2019.

“And here I am, being reelected for another term thanks to you. That’s why I tell you, those who have done nothing wrong have nothing to fear,” Lula added.

In 2021, Brazil’s Supreme Court overturned the cases handled by former Judge Sergio Moro, recognizing that he had been biased in the investigation involving Lula. Today, Moro is the governor-elect for the Liberal Party – or PL – the party of Flávio Bolsonaro, with whom he is allied.

item.title: Aircraft carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family lands in US
item.description:
The plane that departed from Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, representing Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board landed shortly before 10:30 a.m. Brasília time on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at Opa-Locka Airport in Miami, US.

According to the real-time flight tracking website Flight Aware, the trip lasted about four hours.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape.
Flávio, his wife, and daughters crossed the border into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones.

At 11:30 p.m., the family boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

item.title: Plane carrying Flávio Bolsonaro and his family heads to Miami
item.description:
The aircraft that departed Ecuador with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (of the Liberal Party, or PL, for Rio de Janeiro state) and his family on board is currently en route to Miami International Airport in the US. According to the real-time flight tracking website Flight Aware, the plane should land on US soil around 10:20 a.m. Brasília time.

Flávio Bolsonaro, his wife, and daughters crossed the border into Argentina at 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday (Oct. 27) via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones. At 11:30 p.m., the family boarded a private plane bound for Guayaquil, Ecuador. The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
On Tuesday, a close ally of Flávio Bolsonaro and a US government source confirmed to Reuters that the senator had fled to the US. Flávio failed to meet the deadline set by Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Court to surrender his passports to the Federal Police.

The day before, in a video posted on social media after being summoned by the judiciary, Flávio had denied any intention of leaving Brazil and said he would remain in the country to, as he put it, organize opposition to the government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who was reelected on Sunday (26) after defeating the senator in the second round of the presidential election.

item.title: Campaign coordinator says he was surprised by Flávio’s escape
item.description:
Senator Rogério Marinho of the Liberal Party (PL), who coordinated Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, told the press on Tuesday (Oct. 27) that he was unaware of Flávio and his family’s departure for the US.

“We are surprised because yesterday we discussed the need for Flávio - with the 60 million votes he received - to take on a leadership role in the opposition, which is important because, in our assessment, we have a government that has clearly been harmful to the country,” said Marinho after attending a meeting with lawmakers and political leaders from the PL in Brasília.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador.
  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro’s party acknowledges Lula’s victory.
Marinho also mentioned that he had received a text message from Flávio Bolsonaro around 8 a.m. on Tuesday (27), in which he said he was going to “take some time off” and would later speak with his allies again.

The undisclosed trip to the US, whose details remain unknown, took place less than 48 hours after he lost the presidential election to Lula. The move was reported by Reuters and confirmed by a US government official.

Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil, including Senator-elect Carlos Jordy (PL – Rio de Janeiro), have issued statements confirming his departure.

“Confirmed! Flávio Bolsonaro went to the US to avoid being used as a bargaining chip in efforts to impeach Moraes!” said Jordy, referring to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

Despite this, no official from Brazil or the US has made a public statement about his departure.

Investigations

Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation by the Federal Police in several cases involving alleged crimes such as currency evasion, money laundering, and corruption. His term as senator for Rio de Janeiro ends in February 2027, when he will lose his special jurisdiction.

Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered on Monday (26) that the former candidate surrender his passports to the police; however, the documents were not handed over.

The court order is part of the case in which Flávio Bolsonaro and attorney Willer Tomaz are being investigated by the Supreme Court for money laundering.

Due to his failure to comply with the order, the Federal Police revoked the senator’s passports.

In a video posted on Monday, Flávio denied that he had plans to leave the country and said he would turn in his passports.

Agência Brasil contacted Flávio Bolsonaro’s press office but received no response.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro crosses Argentine border, heads to Ecuador
item.description:
Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Liberal Party), his wife, Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and their two daughters, Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro, entered Argentina on Tuesday night (Oct. 27). The information was confirmed by Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration.

In a statement, the agency specified that they crossed the border at 10:50 p.m. via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge in the province of Misiones. At 11:30 p.m., according to the Argentine government, Flávio and his family boarded a private plane operated by Baires Fly and flew to Guayaquil, Ecuador, as indicated in the flight plan.

Notícias relacionadas:

  • Federal Police revoke Flávio Bolsonaro’s passports.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro rejects Lula’s victory, seeks to annul election.
  • Flávio Bolsonaro fled to US, Reuters reports.
Also, Argentina’s National Directorate of Migration stated that the four presented valid travel documents and faced no legal impediment to entering the country. “The crossing was recorded by immigration authorities without incident,” the agency reported.
